title: רב כהנא

paragraphs: Rav Kahana, Rav Yosef's colleague, before Rav Yehudah. Rav Yosef said: Rav Kahana said, 'When we were at Rav Yehudah's,' chapter HaDar (67, end of side b); this is how it should read. Rav Yosef behind Rav Kahana, and Rav Kahana before Rav Yehudah, Yevamot (17a). He visited Rav Yosef's house, Nedarim (22b). He said, 'Rav Yehudah said,' Mo'ed Katan (8a). He recited before Rav Yehudah, Yoma (11a). Rav Kahana objected against Rav Yehudah, Beitzah (33, beginning of side b). R. Abba sat behind Rav Kahana, who sat before Rav Yehudah, Ḥullin (19b). Accordingly it appears there were three undesignated Rav Kahanas: the first, mentioned above, Rav's student-colleague; this one who sat before Rav Yehudah, spoke in his name, recited before him and challenged him; and the third, teacher of the later Rav Ashi. Rav Ashi visited Rav Kahana's house and said, 'Let the master come up to us to complete five.' Rav Kahana said, 'I was standing before Rav Yehudah, who told me: Come up and join a group of five,' Yevamot (101, end of side b). This appears to be the early Rav Ashi, and Rav Kahana here Rav Yehudah's student, since the first Rav Kahana was Rav's student-colleague, while Rav Yehudah was Rav's full student: how could Rav's student-colleague become Rav Yehudah's student? Rav Kahana (the last), Rabbah's student (in my opinion it should read Rava), Rav Ashi's teacher, was a priest; see above, the early Rav Kahana. He and Rav Safra were studying Sanhedrin before Rabbah (it requires examination whether this should read Rava). Rami bar Ḥama encountered them; they said, 'Through the master's kindness we say much of it; through the master's rebuke we say not even one [thing],' Sanhedrin (41b). Rav Ashi knew testimony for Rav Kahana, Ketubbot (20, beginning of side b). Rav Ashi said, 'Rav Kahana and I signed the deed of Ze'iri the orphan's mother,' Gittin (52b). Rav Ashi said, 'When we were at Rav Kahana's,' Ellu Terefot (49a), Bava Kamma (95b). 'I saw Rav Kahana take two [loaves] and break one'; R. Zeira broke [enough] for the whole meal, Shabbat (117, end of side b). Rav Ashi sat before Rav Kahana. It grew late and the rabbis had not come. He asked why: perhaps they were occupied with the Purim meal. He said, 'Should they not have eaten it at night?' He answered, 'Has the master not heard Rava's statement?' etc. He said, 'Did Rava say that?' He learned it from him forty times, Megillah (7b). Tosafot, Menaḥot (102a), reads, 'Rav Ashi said: I stated this teaching before Rav Kahana.' This is the last Rav Kahana, who lived in Rav Ashi's days, as in many places; see there. So too Zevaḥim (106): Rav Ashi said, 'I stated this teaching before Rav Kahana.' Rav Ashi said, 'When I was at Rav Kahana's he told us,' Berakhot (39a, 42a), Yevamot, chapter 1, Shabbat (150b). Rav Ashi called him 'master': 'Does the master not accept Rava's statement?' Sukkah (7a, 19a, 22a), Shabbat (136a). Rav Kahana said to Rav Ashi, 'Rava said the law follows Shemuel; what about here?' He answered, 'Did he weave them all in one weave?' Berakhot (24a). One of the rabbis asked Rav Kahana, 'Why are you not regularly before Rav Pappa and Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua?' Chapter Rabbi Akiva (89). Rav Kahana fell ill; the rabbis sent Rav Yehoshua bar Rav Idi, who found he had died, Pesaḥim (3b). This appears to be the second Rav Kahana (meaning the third), for Rav Idi, R. Yehoshua's father, lived in Rava's time, Rav Pappa was Rava's student, and Rav Pappa spoke to the later Rav Ashi. Thus R. Yehoshua plainly lived in the second (third) Rav Kahana's days. (See above, part 1 [ח״א, provisional], where he became head in year 4143, for twenty-eight years.) Rav Kahana escorted Rav Shimi bar Ashi from Pum Nahara to Bei Tzinyata of Babylonia, which date from Adam, Berakhot (31a), Sotah (46b). Examine: this is the second (third) Rav Kahana. Between Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi, the law follows Rav Kahana (Halikhot Olam, gate 2, פ׳ [locator unresolved]).

Since Tosafot holds there were two Rav Kahanas, while Yuḥasin divided them into three—the early one, Rav's student-colleague; one who was Rav Yehudah's student and Rav Yosef's colleague; and the last, Rav Ashi's teacher—and they are mentioned without further designation, I have arranged their teachers, colleagues and students together. You must understand and discern whom they spoke with, according to the generation.

R. Abba, his student (see above, the second Rav Kahana). R. Abba bar Yosef bar Rava (the last Rav Kahana). R. Abbahu, his teacher (the first Rav Kahana). R. Adda Karḥinai before him (the last Rav Kahana). R. Aḥa said: Rav Kahana said. Rav Aḥa bar Rav Huna. He healed Rav Aḥa bar Rav Yosef of jaundice—apparently the last Rav Kahana. Rav Assi, colleague of the early Rav Kahana. For the last Rav Kahana, see Rav Bivi bar Abaye. He said, 'Rav Giddel said.' Rav Huna, colleague of the early Rav Kahana, according to Yuḥasin; yet this requires examination, since Rav Huna was Rav's student while Rav Kahana was like Rav's student-colleague. Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua: the last Rav Kahana. Rav Huna bar Rav Ika, his colleague. He spoke to Rav Zevid and eulogized him. Before Rav Zevid of Nehardea. Ze'eira said: Rav Kahana said. Ze'eira said: the early Rav Kahana said. Ḥizkiyah, his teacher. R. Ḥiyya bar Abba, in the early Rav Kahana's time. R. Ḥelbo. R. Ḥama, the son of Ḥasa's daughter, spoke to him. Rav Ḥanan of Nehardea. Tavi, in his name. Rav Yehudah, teacher of the second Rav Kahana. He said, 'R. Yoḥanan said,' chapter Rabbi Akiva (85b): the early Rav Kahana. Rav Yosef, in his name, Menaḥot (32a), Yevamot (102a). Rav Yeimar objected against the last Rav Kahana. R. Yannai son of R. Yosef bar Rava—this requires examination. R. Yitzḥak called him 'my teacher.' Rav Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta before him. Rav Yitzḥak bar Rav Yehudah (see Rav Aḥa bar Rav Huna). R. Yirmeyah of Difti objected against him. In R. Yishmael son of R. Yose's name: the first Rav Kahana. He told Mar, Ravina's son, that at eighteen he had mastered the entire Shas but did not know that Scripture does not depart from its plain sense, Shabbat (63a). It is uncertain whether this is the last Kahana, or perhaps the first, who lived long. Rav Mesharshya bar Ḥaklai, in his time. R. Nanai son of R. Yosef bar Rava. Rav Safra: the last Rav Kahana. In Ulla's name, HaMaddir (74a). In R. Akiva's name, Sanhedrin (76a–b): the early Rav Kahana. He spoke to Rav Pappa and Rav Pappi. In Rava's name: the last Rav Kahana. Rava bar Ittai. Rabbah, his student. Rabbah, in his name, Menaḥot (32a). Rabbah, his teacher: the last Rav Kahana. Rabbah bar Sheva before him. Rami bar Ḥama encountered him (see above). Rav Sheva said to him. Shila Mari. Before Rav Shima. In Shimi bar Ashi's name: the last Rav Kahana. R. Shemuel bar Shilat, in his name. Rav Shemuel bar Rabbah bar bar Ḥana. R. Shimon son of Rabbi, in the first Rav Kahana's time. R. Yirmeyah said: Kahana asked Resh Lakish, etc.; R. Yose bar Bun said, 'Here Kahana spread his net over Resh Lakish and caught him,' Jerusalem Talmud, Kilayim, chapter 1, halakhah 6. He said, 'Resh Lakish said,' Shabbat (63a): the early Rav Kahana. R. Tanḥum bar Ḥiyya bar Abba.
